question: The position vectors of points $P$ and $R$ are $2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and $4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, respectively. The point $R$ divides the line segment joining $P$ to an unknown point $Q$ internally in the ratio $2:3$. Determine the position vector of $Q$ and verify using vector components that $P$, $R$ and $Q$ are collinear in the stated order.
explanation: Applying the Section FormulaLet the position vectors of $P$, $Q$ and $R$ be $\vec{p}$, $\vec{q}$ and $\vec{r}$, respectively. Since $R$ divides $PQ$ internally in the ratio $2:3$,`\vec{r}=\frac{2\vec{q}+3\vec{p}}{5}`Therefore,`2\vec{q}=5\vec{r}-3\vec{p}`Substituting the given vectors,`2\vec{q}=5(4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-\hat{k})-3(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k})2\vec{q}=(20\hat{i}+15\hat{j}-5\hat{k})-(6\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+9\hat{k})2\vec{q}=14\hat{i}+18\hat{j}-14\hat{k}`Thus,`\vec{q}=7\hat{i}+9\hat{j}-7\hat{k}`Verification of Collinearity and Order`\overrightarrow{PR}=\vec{r}-\vec{p}\overrightarrow{PR}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-4\hat{k}`Also,`\overrightarrow{RQ}=\vec{q}-\vec{r}\overrightarrow{RQ}=3\hat{i}+6\hat{j}-6\hat{k}`Therefore,`\overrightarrow{RQ}=\frac{3}{2}\overrightarrow{PR}`The positive scalar multiplier shows that both vectors have the same direction. Hence, $P$, $R$ and $Q$ are collinear, with $R$ lying between $P$ and $Q$. Moreover,`PR:RQ=2:3`Final ResultThe position vector of $Q$ is $7\hat{i}+9\hat{j}-7\hat{k}$, and the required collinearity and division ratio are verified.
